result.title: InferPriv: Evaluating Inferential Privacy Leakage in LLM Assistants
result.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based personal agents are increasingly deployed to handle everyday tasks on users' behalf. These agents have access to private user information, while their tasks involve communicating with third parties; this raises a critical privacy concern that agents may inappropriately reveal sensitive user information to these recipients. Existing benchmarks primarily assess direct privacy leakage, where an agent explicitly states a pre-specified secret or attribute. However, they do not capture \textit{inferential leakage}, where the model leaves indirect cues in the reply that implicitly leaks sensitive attributes. We introduce \textsc{InferPriv}, a benchmark that measures whether an honest-but-curious recipient can infer a user's sensitive attributes from an LLM's reply on routine task. Evaluating five frontier models, we find that inferential leakage substantially exceeds direct leakage across models and prompts. Under a privacy-aware system prompt, GPT-6.1-Sol, Sonnet-5.5, and Gemini-3.8-Flash achieve near-zero direct leakage, yet the inferential leakage rate remains between 16.2--25.2\%. These findings suggest that evaluating explicit leakage alone can substantially understate the privacy risks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 InferPriv 基准，用「诚实但好奇的接收方」从 LLM 助手回复中推断用户敏感属性的方式，度量任务回复里的间接（推断式）隐私泄露，并发现其显著高于直接泄露，即便有隐私约束提示也仍有 16.2–25.2%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由下游推断者反推回复中隐含信息」的评估协议，可供核查 LVR 中答案或 latent 状态是否隐含保留视觉细节与任务必要信息，作为信息坍缩的间接探针；但该文针对文本隐私，需评估迁移到视觉状态的有效性。
